newsitem.title: USA: Volvo acquires GM equity interest in truck venture.
newsitem.headline: Volvo acquires GM equity interest in truck venture.

text.p: Swedish automaker AB Volvo said Wednesday it bought General Motors Corp.'s remaining equity interest in Volvo GM Heavy Truck Corp. and will change the U.S. truckmaker's name to Volvo Trucks North America.

GM exchanged its 13 percent common stock interest in the Greensboro, N.C.-based truck maker for an undisclosed amount of preferred stock, from which it will receive dividends, said GM spokeswoman Toni Simonetti.

GM will retain one seat on the unit's board of directors, and will continue to sell its medium-duty trucks through the Volvo Trucks North America dealer network, she said. Volvo Trucks, which builds heavy tractor-trailer type trucks, also will change the name of its Canadian affiliate to eliminate the GM name.

"We are now Volvo," Marc Gustafson, president and chief executive officer of Volvo Trucks, said in a statement. "This investment is a concrete sign of Volvo's commitment to the North American truck market.
"Volvo Trucks is poised to build a stronger organization which will enable it to achieve the same level of success as its parent has in other parts of the world," he added.
Philip Romba, a Volvo Trucks spokesman in Greensboro, said no major changes in the company's North American manufacturing, sales and administrative functions were anticipated as a result of the deal.

Volvo entered the U.S. heavy truck market in 1981 when it purchased assets of the bankrupt White Motor Co. In 1988, it combined those assets with GM's heavy truck business, creating Volvo GM Heavy Truck Corp., which at the time was 76 percent owned by Volvo and 24 percent by GM.
Equity infusions by Volvo subsequently diluted GM's stake.
The venture marketed trucks under the White-GMC name until 1995, when it switched to the Volvo name on all of its products.
